question: Who is not qualified to use the 8% income tax rate?
reference_answer: Not qualified: purely compensation income earners; VAT-registered taxpayers; non-VAT taxpayers whose gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income exceeded the P3,000,000 VAT threshold; taxpayers subject to Other Percentage Taxes under Title V (except Sec. 116); partners of a General Professional Partnership; and individuals enjoying income tax exemption such as BMBE-registered taxpayers.

question: What are the main differences between the graduated income tax rates and the 8% income tax rate?
reference_answer: Graduated rates apply to all individuals and are based on net taxable income, with itemized deductions or OSD allowed, and the taxpayer is subject to percentage tax or VAT. The 8% rate is only for qualified individuals in business/profession whose gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income did not exceed P3,000,000; it is based on gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income, allows only the P250,000 reduction for purely self-employed individuals, and the taxpayer is not subject to percentage tax.

question: How do I avail of the 8% income tax rate and when is the deadline to choose it?
reference_answer: Signify the option through BIR Form 1901 (new registrants) or the initial quarterly return, or for existing taxpayers via BIR Form 1905, the 1st quarter percentage tax return, or the 1st quarter income tax return. The election must be made annually on or before May 15 and is irrevocable for that year, unless gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income exceed P3,000,000, in which case the graduated rates automatically apply.

question: What happens if I qualify for the 8% rate but forgot to signify that I chose it?
reference_answer: A qualified individual who failed to signify the intention to avail of the 8% rate is subject to the graduated income tax rates.

question: I'm a purely self-employed freelancer on the 8% rate. Do I still need to file and pay the 3% percentage tax?
reference_answer: No. The 8% income tax is in lieu of both the graduated income tax rates and the percentage tax under Section 116, so a purely self-employed individual who opted for 8% no longer files or pays the 3% percentage tax.

question: What is the 8% income tax based on?
reference_answer: It is based on gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income, net of returns and cash discounts. Individuals earning purely from business or practice of profession may first reduce this by P250,000.

question: I'm employed and I also freelance. Can I deduct the P250,000 from my freelance income if I choose the 8% rate?
reference_answer: No. Only individuals earning purely from self-employment/practice of profession get the P250,000 reduction. Mixed income earners are not entitled to it on their business income because the amount was already applied in computing the tax on compensation.

question: When filing my quarterly return on the 8% rate, should I subtract P62,500 (P250,000 divided by 4) each quarter?
reference_answer: No. There is no need to divide the P250,000 into four quarters; the quarterly income tax return (Form 1701Q) uses a cumulative quarterly computation that already accounts for the reduction.

question: What tax rates apply if I earn both a salary and income from my own business or profession?
reference_answer: Compensation income is subject to the graduated rates. Business/professional income is subject to graduated rates or, if qualified and at the taxpayer's option, the 8% rate on gross sales/receipts.

question: Is a security deposit I receive under a lease part of my gross receipts?
reference_answer: In general all deposits are included in gross receipts, but returnable deposits or deposits held in trust and recorded as a liability are excluded.

question: Am I considered self-employed if I work under a contract of service or job order?
reference_answer: Yes. An individual under a contract of service or job order arrangement is considered self-employed.

question: My only client pays me less than P250,000 a year. Can I avoid having income tax withheld on my fees?
reference_answer: Yes. If annual gross receipts from a lone payor will not exceed P250,000, the payee may be exempt from withholding tax on income by submitting a Sworn Declaration of Gross Receipts/Sales (Annex B-2 of RR 11-2018) together with a copy of the Certificate of Registration (COR) or BIR Form 1901.

question: Why do I need to give my client a copy of my Certificate of Registration with my sworn declaration?
reference_answer: The COR lets the withholding agent confirm that the payee is registered with the BIR and is a non-VAT taxpayer who may qualify for the 8% rate if gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income did not exceed P3M.

question: What withholding tax rate applies to self-employed individuals who are not classified as professionals?
reference_answer: If the service is not covered by the definition of a professional and does not fall under Section 2.57.2(A) of RR 2-98 as amended by RR 11-2018, it is subject to 2% withholding.

question: What withholding tax rate do individual contractors face?
reference_answer: Individual contractors are subject to creditable expanded withholding tax at 2%.

question: As a consultant who submitted the sworn declaration, will my withholding rate differ depending on whether I chose 8% or graduated rates?
reference_answer: No. The withholding rate for doctors/consultants who submitted the sworn declaration is 5% regardless of whether they chose the 8% or graduated rates. A government payor also withholds business tax if the payee chose graduated rates.

question: What rate will my client withhold from my professional fees if I don't submit a sworn declaration?
reference_answer: 10% income tax. If the payor is a government entity, the payment is also subject to 3% percentage tax or 5% withholding VAT, whichever applies.

question: What certificate should my client give me for taxes withheld under a job order or contract of service?
reference_answer: BIR Form 2307 (Certificate of Creditable Tax Withheld at Source), since the tax withheld is a creditable withholding tax.

question: Do I need to attach financial statements to my annual income tax return if I'm on the 8% rate?
reference_answer: No. Financial statements are not required to be attached for those who opt and qualify for the 8% rate.

question: I chose graduated rates with the Optional Standard Deduction. Do I need to submit financial statements?
reference_answer: No. A taxpayer who opts for OSD under the graduated rates is exempt from submitting financial statements.

question: If I'm on graduated rates, when is my 3% percentage tax due?
reference_answer: File a quarterly percentage tax return and pay the 3% tax within twenty-five (25) days after the end of each taxable quarter.

question: When must my client give me Form 2307?
reference_answer: On or before the 20th day after the close of the quarter, or upon demand of the payee.

question: What are the deadlines for filing BIR Form 1701Q?
reference_answer: 1st quarter on or before May 15, 2nd quarter on or before August 15, and 3rd quarter on or before November 15 of the current taxable year.

question: What happens if I don't mark a deduction method on my quarterly income tax return?
reference_answer: The taxpayer is deemed to have chosen itemized deductions, and the choice is irrevocable for the taxable year.

question: How much is the Optional Standard Deduction for individuals?
reference_answer: A maximum of 40% of gross sales or receipts, in lieu of itemized deductions; individuals who use OSD need not submit financial statements.

question: What is the graduated income tax rate on taxable income between P400,000 and P800,000 starting 2023?
reference_answer: From January 1, 2023 onwards: P22,500 plus 20% of the excess over P400,000.

question: What should I attach to my quarterly income tax return if clients withheld tax from my payments?
reference_answer: Attach the Certificate of Creditable Tax Withheld at Source (BIR Form 2307), and the Summary Alphalist of Withholding Agents (SAWT) if applicable.

question: Under the EOPT Act, what qualifies me as a micro taxpayer?
reference_answer: Micro taxpayers are those with gross sales of less than P3,000,000.

question: I'm on the 8% rate. Can I deduct my rent and internet bills as business expenses?
reference_answer: No. Individuals who opted for the 8% income tax rate on their business/professional income are not allowed any deductions; the 8% tax is computed on gross sales/receipts and other non-operating income (less P250,000 if purely self-employed).

question: Where can I file and pay my quarterly income tax return?
reference_answer: Under the EOPT Act, taxpayers can file returns and pay taxes, electronically or manually, with any Authorized Agent Bank, Revenue District Office (through its Revenue Collection Officers), or Authorized Tax Software Provider — file and pay anywhere, without penalties for filing at the wrong venue.
